title: Orchestrated on-prem upgrade quarantine and tenant recovery for asymmetric helm hook failures
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: During a staged on-prem Helm upgrade for multiple VPC customers, several tenants entered degraded state due to asymmetric execution of Helm pre/post hooks and a timing window where the operator leader-election moved controllers between nodes. This ticket coordinates the hotfix, runbook updates, and customer recovery steps for affected tenants. The issue was first reported by two enterprise customers experiencing control-plane failures and model-serving stalls after operator rollout.
impact: Multiple tenants on Dedicated/Private saw pod restart loops, webhook 500s and stalled CR reconcilers for 3–18 minutes. Customer-facing inference endpoints returned 503s intermittently; three customers (Acme Health, NovaRetail, FinArc) filed escalations and required support intervention. SLA blips recorded in our uptime dashboard; billing unaffected but customer confidence impacted.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Prepare on-prem cluster with operator v3.1.9, tenants with pinned tenant-configs and custom admission webhooks. 2) Trigger helm upgrade to operator v3.2.1 with default hooks enabled and use rolling update strategy. 3) Observe operator leader-election logs and helm hook logs; in ~40% of test runs the post-upgrade mutatingWebhookConfiguration was removed before node agents reconciled, causing admission failures and CR queue stall. 4) Reproduce by adding artificial leader-election delay (kill controller leader) during helm post-upgrade hook window.
root_cause: Race between Helm hooks that modify mutatingWebhookConfiguration and operator leader-election/leader-transfer logic. In certain upgrade orders, Helm removed a webhook CA bundle as part of a values change before the new node-agent re-registered certificates. When operator leadership shifted, some controller replicas attempted writes against CRs without a valid webhook registration and failed reconcile, leaving CRs in a pending state. Secondary factor: a previously missing retry/backoff on helm-hook idempotency allowed partial state to persist.
mitigation: 1) Emergency hotfix (operator-3.2.1-hotfix-rc1) introduced: a safe-update wrapper around Helm hooks that delays webhook removal until nodeagent health-checks report certificate presence; additional idempotency guards for hook execution. 2) Runbook step: quiesce helm upgrades for clusters with >50 tenants until hotfix applied. 3) Per-tenant recovery script added to operator toolbox: detect pending CRs, patch webhook CA in place, and force reconcile safely. 4) Incident support runbook enacted; customer-facing communication sent via SEs.

resolution: Hotfix merged and backported to release-3.x (PR #1876). Release 3.2.2 scheduled; customers with >50 tenants requested assisted upgrades. Runbook updated to include preflight checks for webhook CA presence and leader-election quiescing. Post-deploy checks added to console to surface webhook registration latency.
monitoring_changes: Trace: leader-election.transfer.duration histogram added to console trace panel
postmortem_summary: The incident was caused by a coordination gap between Helm hook sequencing and operator leader-election during rolling upgrades. Hotfixes added defensiveness around hook operations and improved preflight checks. The event exposed limits in our upgrade gating for large-multi-tenant private clusters. No data loss occurred; customer impact limited to degraded availability for short windows. Recommendations: strengthen preflight, expand chaos tests, and introduce a short global pause window for leader-election during critical helm hook windows.

Increase test coverage of helm-hook idempotency and add property-based tests for partial hook runs
Customer outreach: schedule 1:1 upgrade walk-throughs with top 10 affected accounts
notes: Avoids duplicating wording used in prior helm/operator tickets: focuses on quarantine + tenant recovery rather than generic upgrade hotfix wording.
